rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3 and Table 2 - the authors acquired a Hyperion image over Mackay (2 April 2002), digitised 142 rust-affected and 159 non-affected sample pixels, computed 40 spectral indices and ran discriminant function analysis with a 30% hold-out sample; their own result is that DWSI-1, DWSI-2, DWSI-5 and MSI gave the best discrimination and a combined function reached 96.9% hold-out accuracy.
rows.notes: The study's own result is limited to detecting/discriminating sugarcane blocks with moderate-to-high severity orange rust from non-diseased blocks in one Hyperion scene. It does not report any result on farmers taking action, on control or prevention of further damage, or on any downstream outcome; disease management and chemical application are only mentioned in the Introduction as motivation. Detection is a precondition of the claimed pest-control effect, so Q2 is 'no' and upstream is set. For the detection step itself the study reports a standard deviation of spectra (Figure 3), notes limitations (only severity-4 fields assessed, early-stage detection untested, water-stressed but non-diseased crops could confound the indices, single region/scene), and uses one method (imagery vs field officer ratings as reference), but none of this counts toward the claimed control effect.

notes: Full text appears complete (short Letter, 10 pages including references). Single site, single date, single variety (Q124); classification accuracies are reported but no uncertainty on the claimed control effect because that effect is not studied.
